sections.h2: What are the ways to sell a house fast in Temple Terrace?
sections.html:
You can list with an agent, sell to a cash buyer, or negotiate a direct sale with a neighbor or investor. Each route trades price against speed, and Temple Terrace gives you a few local reasons to weigh them carefully.

The city sits just outside Tampa in Hillsborough County, close to the University of South Florida and the Hillsborough River. Because the city is compact and close to a major university, many buyers here are investors who want a quick, clean closing.

  • Traditional listing: the widest buyer pool, but showings, repairs and a buyer's lender timeline can stretch the process.
  • Cash offer: fewer contingencies and a closing date you choose, usually at a lower price than a fully prepared listing.
  • Sale of an inherited or tenant-occupied house: the title or the lease usually decides how quickly you can close.

sections.h2: What does Temple Terrace look like for a seller?
sections.html:
Temple Terrace is a small, mostly built-out city of about 7 square miles with a population estimate of 27,075 for July 1, 2025, per Census QuickFacts. The city describes itself as a small-town place with urban amenities, and its own site dates the city to 1925.

The same QuickFacts page lists 11,630 households, and about half of housing units are owner-occupied (50.4 percent for 2020 to 2024). That is a low owner share for a Florida suburb, so a good number of buyers and sellers here are investors or landlords. The reported median value of owner-occupied homes is $334,800, and median gross rent is $1,594, both for 2020 to 2024.

sections.h2: Do Temple Terrace short-term rental rules affect a sale?
sections.html:
Yes, if the house has been rented to guests, the buyer will want to know whether it is registered. The city runs a Short-Term Rental Program for homes rented for fewer than 30 days at a time and more than 3 times a year.

The city program page says every such rental needs a Certificate of Use renewed each year, a fire department life-safety inspection repeated every two years, and a local responsible party reachable at all hours. Violations can go to the Municipal Code Enforcement Board and can bring a civil citation.

  • Occupancy is capped at two persons per bedroom plus two.
  • Guest vehicles must use approved off-street parking, not lawns or rights of way.
  • Quiet hours run 8 p.m. to 8 a.m. Sunday through Thursday and 10 p.m. to 8 a.m. Friday and Saturday.
  • Ads must show the occupancy limit, vehicle limit, state license number or Exempt, and the Certificate of Use number.

If you own a rental, gather the certificate, the latest inspection record and any citations before you accept an offer. An investor who plans to keep renting will ask for them. The city's complaint line printed on that page is 813-501-6769.

sections.h2: Which schools and nearby places help a Temple Terrace listing?
sections.html:
The schools and institutions around the city are a real selling point, and a buyer will recognize them. The city's school page lists Lewis Elementary, Riverhills Elementary and Temple Terrace Elementary, Greco Middle, and King High School in Tampa, plus private options such as Corpus Christi Catholic School and Florida College Academy.

The city's information page also points to Florida College, USF, the Museum of Science and Industry, Busch Gardens, riverfront parks, a public library, a recreation center and a historic golf and country club. Mention the ones closest to your street in your listing or your note to a buyer. Confirm school assignment with the district before you promise a particular school to anyone.

sections.h2: What does it cost to transfer a house in Temple Terrace?
sections.html:
The main transfer charge is Florida documentary stamp tax on the deed, which the Department of Revenue says is 70 cents per $100 of consideration in every county except Miami-Dade. The same page notes that all parties to the document are liable, whichever side agrees to pay it, and it is collected by the county clerk when the deed is recorded.

Hillsborough County's clerk also charges recording fees set in section 28.24 of the Florida Statutes, starting at $5.00 for the first page and $4.00 for each additional page, with added trust fund and technology charges. Your closing statement will total these. Ask the title company for the final figure before you sign.

  • Deed doc stamps: 70 cents per $100 as printed by the Department of Revenue.
  • Recording: clerk charges per page under s. 28.24.
  • Prorated property tax for the part of the year you owned the home.

sections.h2: How do Hillsborough County property taxes work when I sell?
sections.html:
Florida values property each January 1, mails a proposed tax notice in August, and sends bills in November, according to the Department of Revenue's taxpayer page. Early payment earns a discount of 4 percent in November, falling by one point each month to 1 percent in February.

Taxes you owe for the year of closing are usually split between you and the buyer on the settlement statement. Your homestead exemption ends with the sale, and the buyer's first assessment resets to just value on the next January 1 after the change of ownership. That reset means the buyer's bill can differ sharply from yours, so do not quote your own tax amount as what the buyer will pay.

For current millage and your parcel's figures, ask the Hillsborough County Property Appraiser and Tax Collector.

sections.h2: What if the Temple Terrace house is in foreclosure, probate or has tax problems?
sections.html:
A fast sale is still possible, but each situation has its own deadline. In a judicial foreclosure the court's final judgment sets a public sale between 20 and 35 days later, and the winning bidder pays a 5 percent deposit, so selling before the sale date is the only way to keep control of the price.

For an inherited house, Florida allows summary administration when the non-exempt estate is $150,000 or less or the owner died more than two years ago. A personal representative's deed under a probated will is listed by the Department of Revenue as not taxable for doc stamps. If back taxes are unpaid, the tax collector sells certificates on delinquent accounts, and a holder may apply for a tax deed after two years. Talk to a Florida attorney or title agent about your specific facts.

faqs.q: How fast can a house sell in Temple Terrace?
faqs.a: A cash sale can close in a couple of weeks when the title is clean and the buyer needs no loan. A listed sale usually takes longer because of showings, inspections and a lender's timeline.

faqs.q: Do I pay documentary stamp tax when I sell in Temple Terrace?
faqs.a: The Department of Revenue says all parties to the deed are liable, whichever side agrees to pay. The rate printed for Hillsborough County is 70 cents per $100 of consideration, so settle who pays it in the contract.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Temple Terrace house that I have rented on Airbnb?
faqs.a: Yes. Provide the Certificate of Use, the fire inspection record and any city citations. Buyers who want to keep renting need the registration to stay in good standing.

faqs.q: What happens to my homestead exemption when I sell?
faqs.a: It ends. The exemption requires the home to be your permanent residence, and a change of ownership resets the property to just value the following January 1. You may be able to carry part of the Save Our Homes benefit to a new Florida homestead through portability within three years, filed with the property appraiser.

faqs.q: Where do I record the deed for a Temple Terrace house?
faqs.a: Deeds are recorded with the Hillsborough County clerk of the circuit court. The clerk collects the doc stamp tax and the per-page recording fees at the time of recording.
